title: Short-row boomerang shawl
subtitle: A fingering-weight asymmetric shawl shaped entirely by German short rows.
excerpt: An asymmetric boomerang-shaped shawl in fingering-weight wool worked flat, shaped entirely by German short rows rather than yarn-over increases or decreases. The result is a curved wedge that fits naturally over the back of the neck. Wingspan approximately 175 cm, maximum depth approximately 50 cm. About 350 g of fingering yarn.
sourceNotes: The boomerang shawl shape using short rows is a contemporary design form with no single period source. German short rows (double stitch method) are documented in Stephanie Pearl-McPhee, Knitting Rules! (2006) and widely adopted in modern knitwear design as a cleaner alternative to wrap-and-turn short rows.

knitting.gaugeText: 24 sts × 48 rows = 10 × 10 cm in garter stitch on 3.75 mm needles, blocked.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Wingspan approximately 175 cm. Maximum depth approximately 50 cm. Blocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: A short row technique where, when turning, the first stitch is slipped purlwise with the yarn in front, then the yarn is brought over the needle to the back, pulling the slipped stitch up into a double stitch (two loops on one needle). On the return row, the double stitch is knitted or purled through both loops together as one stitch.

content.text: A fingering shawl shaped entirely by
German short rows
rather than yarn-over increases. Wingspan about 175 cm, depth about 50 cm.

The shawl is cast on at the centre back and worked outward in two wings, each shaped by progressively longer short rows that build up the body from the neck edge outward. The German short row method creates a clean turn with no holes. Budget about 350 g (about 1,400 m / 1,530 yards) of fingering wool.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: About 350 g (1,400 m / 1,530 yards) of fingering-weight yarn

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, 80 cm or longer

content.text: Gauge

24 stitches and 48 rows to 10 cm over garter stitch on 3.75 mm needles, blocked. Because the boomerang shape depends on short row counts rather than stitch count, gauge affects the wingspan (stitch count determines width) but the depth accumulates via row count. At gauge each set of 2 short rows adds approximately 2 mm of depth.
Stitches used

items.name: DS
items.qty: German double stitch: slip 1 purlwise, bring yarn over needle to back, pulling a double loop

items.name: k-DS
items.qty: knit the double stitch: knit both legs of the DS together through the front loop

content.text: Pattern
Cast on
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 420 stitches (the full wingspan at 24 sts / 10 cm for 175 cm). Tail: approximately (3.75 × 420) / 10 + 15 = 172.5 cm. Place a centre marker after stitch 210.
Short row section
Row 1 (RS): k to 8 sts before centre marker, turn with DS.
Row 2 (WS): k to 8 sts before opposite edge, turn with DS.
Row 3: k to DS from row 1, k-DS, k8, turn with DS.
Row 4: k to DS from row 2, k-DS, k8, turn with DS.
Continue, always knitting past the previous DS and adding 8 more stitches before the new turn. Repeat until all stitches are included in the active knitting and both DS turns reach the shawl edges.
Finishing rows
Work 4 full-width garter rows across all 420 stitches to neaten the edge.
Bind off
Work Jeny's surprisingly stretchy bind-off across all 420 stitches. This is the long curved bottom edge of the boomerang.
Stitch count check-ins

After every 10 short row pairs: the active knitting width grows by approximately 16 stitches per wing (8 per side). At 26 short row pairs each wing has grown by 208 stitches, reaching the full cast-on width.
Common faults

German double stitch leaking holes: the double stitch was not pulled tightly enough over the needle when made. When creating a DS, pull the yarn firmly over the needle tip before continuing to knit; the double loop should sit snugly against the needle.
Boomerang curve not symmetrical: the short row increments were different on the two sides. The increment must be the same (8 stitches) on every turn for both RS and WS rows.
Blocking
Wet-block to wingspan 175 cm and maximum depth 50 cm. The boomerang curve is set by the short row construction and will be visible before blocking; pinning simply opens the garter structure.
Care
Hand wash in cool water, lay flat to dry.
What to try next
Add a lace stitch pattern across the full width on every full-width row in the set of finishing rows for a simple lace finish at the cast-off edge.
